transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Lee. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Um... hi. I guess my eating has just gotten really off lately. Some days I barely get down some coffee and a granola bar before a shift. And... my scrubs have been hanging pretty loose on me. I'm not actually trying to lose weight or anything, it's just happening. So... yeah, I guess that's why I'm here.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed your mood feeling down, or have you lost interest or pleasure in things you normally enjoy?
Yeah, I guess so. Most mornings I just... wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling. Like the day is already ruined before I even put my badge on. So, yeah. It's been down.
How long have you been feeling this way—waking up with that heavy, hollow feeling and low mood—has it been going on for two weeks or more, or is it more recent?
Um... it's been more than two weeks. It kind of... settled in a while ago. I guess it's been with me for about a year and four months now.
Have you noticed any other physical changes recently, like your heart racing, feeling unusually hot or sweaty, or your hands shaking?
No, not really. I haven't noticed anything like that. Just... tired, mostly.

When you're eating less, is it because food just doesn't appeal to you or you don't feel hungry, or is it more that you're consciously trying to limit what you eat because of how you feel about your body or weight?

It's not about my weight. I just... I don't really have an appetite. Some days I barely get down coffee and a granola bar before my shift. I haven't been trying to lose anything, but... my scrubs are hanging pretty loose on me lately. Food just doesn't appeal to me much right now.
Over this past year and four months, have there been any stretches of two months or longer where your mood and energy returned to normal before things got low again?

No... not really. I don't think I've had a break that long. For most of this whole stretch, I've just been living with that heavy, hollow mood... and not caring about much. It's not just a few bad weeks here and there. It's just... been there.
I'm not really sure what you're asking... I haven't noticed anything like that.
During this time, have you had thoughts that you'd be better off dead, or found yourself thinking a lot about worthlessness or guilt?

I haven't... I haven't made any kind of plan to hurt myself or anything like that. But I do... sometimes I just catch myself wishing I wouldn't wake up. Or thinking it would just be easier if I disappeared. I don't know.

How has this affected your ability to function at work and in your daily activities—are you still able to get through your shifts and manage daily tasks, or has it become very difficult to keep up with things?

It's... it's been hard. I guess I've been making some mistakes at work. Things I shouldn't mess up. Sometimes people have to tell me things twice... simple things. I just... I don't really go out anymore, either. I used to do chess nights, take walks with my camera... but I just avoid it now. I don't really trust myself to... keep up, or act normal around people. So I just don't go.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep lately—trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual?

It's... broken up. I guess I lie there for a while. Just... replaying things from work. And listening. If there are noises. Then I usually wake up around 3 or 4 in the morning. I just kind of lie there until the alarm goes off. I can't really get back to sleep.
Over these past 16 months, has your mood and functioning stayed at about the same level the whole time, or was there a point where things noticeably got worse than how you'd been feeling before?

It's... pretty much been the same. For most of this whole stretch, I guess. Just... that heavy feeling. Not caring about things. It's not just a bad week here or there. It's... it's just how it is. Most of the time.
